title: Scheduler hotspot + affinity heatmap triage notes
content:
Summary:

On 2026-03-09 ~03:40 UTC we observed a sustained increase in pod schedule latency p95 (from ~250ms baseline to ~3.1s) and a correlated spike in pod preemption/eviction rate in two AZs (us-west-2a and us-west-2c). Customer traffic in hosted API lanes degraded for ~23 minutes while autoscaler and scheduler contended for placement. This doc captures the on-call triage, diagnostics (heatmap/affinity map), temporary mitigations applied, and proposed runbook/runbook edits.

Symptoms observed:
- Pod startup p95 increased from 250ms -> 3.1s between 03:38-04:01 UTC.
- Eviction spike: 480 evictions across cluster in 20m window (normal ~8/min -> observed ~30/min).
- Node utilization pattern: a small subset of nodes (label: hw.gpu=false, ocp-type: general) had CPU steal and kubelet eviction signals.
- Scheduler logs showed repeated scoring ties and several backoff retries due to insufficient allocatable CPU after accounting for reserved system pods.

What made this unusual:
- Affinity and anti-affinity rules from a recent rollout (PR #452) increased soft-affinity weighting for pod groups used by batch jobs, amplifying scheduler bin-packing in a small subset of AZs.
- A CI job concurrently launched synthetic traffic that pinned ephemeral networking (cni) flows to pods on a hot subset of nodes, creating transient packet-burst noise which slowed kube-probe responses and triggered liveness restarts.

Timeline (high level):
- 03:35 UTC: Alert (pod-scheduling-p95) fires.
- 03:36 UTC: On-call (Maya) joins incident channel, escalates to eng-sre rotation.
- 03:38 UTC: Observed eviction spike and pod restart loops on nodes ip-10-0-5-*.
- 03:42 UTC: Pull scheduler logs, generate affinity heatmap, correlate with node metrics.
- 03:44 UTC: Applied temporary mitigation: rollback of affinity weight change (PR revert) and cordon+drain of 3 hot nodes to re-balance.
- 03:56 UTC: Pod p95 returned near baseline; eviction rate declines.
- 04:05 UTC: Uncordoned nodes after kubelet stability confirmed.
- 04:25 UTC: Close initial incident; opened follow-up ticket OPS-987 for root cause investigation and runbook edits.

Diagnostics performed:
1) Affinity heatmap generation:
   - Ran internal tool to map podGroup -> nodeAffinityScore per node over 1h window. Heatmap showed 3 nodes with >90% of affinity-sourced preferred placements for batch-* pods. These nodes had 4x the median number of descheduled/scheduled pods.

2) Scheduler logs (excerpt):
   - time=2026-03-09T03:40:02Z level=info component=kube-scheduler msg="Attempting Fit" pod=batch-worker-77 node=ip-10-0-5-20
   - time=2026-03-09T03:40:02Z level=warn component=kube-scheduler msg="score tie, applying tie-breaker" reasons=[affinityScore resourcePressure]
   - time=2026-03-09T03:40:03Z level=error component=kube-scheduler msg="binding failed: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded"

3) Node metrics snapshot (03:38-03:45 UTC):
   - Node ip-10-0-5-20: cpu_util 78%, iowait 6%, cpu_steal 14%, kubelet_evictions=12
   - Node ip-10-0-5-21: cpu_util 83%, cpu_steal 12%, kubelet_evictions=10
   - Median node CPU util cluster-wide: 44%

4) CNI/network indicators:
   - CNI non-retransmit packet drops increased on nodes above ~70% host CPU steal.
   - Flows from synthetic CI job had persistent NAT mappings to the hot nodes (investigating whether conntrack expiry biased placement).

Root cause hypothesis (combined):
- A recent change to affinity scoring amplified placement pressure, making a small set of nodes the "preferred" targets. At the same time a noisy workload (CI synthetic traffic) pinned network flows to those nodes, causing CPU steal and kubelet probe timeouts. The combined effect created a positive feedback loop: delayed probes -> restarts/evictions -> scheduler churn -> more pods concentrating onto fewer nodes -> higher host-level contention.

Immediate mitigations applied (what worked):
- Rolled back the affinity weight change from PR #452 (03:44 UTC). Reverting immediately reduced scheduler preference pressure.
- Cordoned and drained the 3 most-affected nodes to move batch pods onto healthier nodes, throttling the feedback loop (03:44-03:50 UTC).
- Temporarily lowered preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution (soft affinity) weight to 0 for batch group via emergency feature-flag (03:46 UTC) when quick revert would have been disruptive.
- Added short-term iptables rule to rate-limit CI job flows while we coordinate with CI owners (03:48 UTC).

Why the mitigations helped:
- Reverting affinity removed the artificial skew in scheduler scoring so new pods were more evenly distributed.
- Draining nodes reduced noisy network/memory pressure and allowed kubelet to recover flakiness.

Lessons learned / proposed runbook edits:
1) Scheduler-affinity rollout checklist: any change to scoring weights that could change distribution should go through a small canary (single AZ) + heatmap verification step. Add post-rollout sampling job that generates an affinity heatmap for 1h and alerts on skew ratio > 3x.
2) Add automated detection: heatmap drift detector that evaluates placement entropy per AZ and fires early if entropy drops below threshold.
3) Update runbook: when pod-schedule-p95 > 1s AND eviction-rate > 10/min, run affinity-heatmap + node-hotspot queries before draining to confirm skew origin.
4) CI work: ensure CI synthetic traffic tests set appropriate tolerations/labels so they do not concentrate on prod general-purpose nodes; move heavy synthetic networking to dedicated test pool.
5) Node-level: add kubelet metric threshold for cpu_steal > 10% to trigger short-lived placement freeze for heavy new batch placements to avoid immediate churning.

Action items (owners and target dates):
- Ethan: implement affinity-rollout-canary job + heatmap exporter (target 2026-03-23).
- Priya: add entropy detector alert and runbook snippet (target 2026-03-18).
- Luca: coordinate with CI owners to move synthetic traffic to dedicated pool and produce mitigation plan (target 2026-03-15).
- Maya: update scheduling runbook with the new checklist and sample diagnostic commands (target 2026-03-13).

Runbook snippets and diagnostic commands (for on-call):
- Generate a quick affinity heatmap (internal tool): /usr/local/bin/k8s-affinity-heatmap --namespace batch --window 60m --output /tmp/heatmap.png
- Count recent evictions: kubectl get events --field-selector reason=Evicted --all-namespaces --since=30m | wc -l
- Node steal check: for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name); do echo $n; kubectl top node $n --use-protocol-buffers; kubectl exec -n kube-system -it $(kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kubelet -o name | head -1) -- curl -s http://localhost:10255/stats | jq '.'; done (note: adapt to metrics stack)

Open questions / follow-ups for RCA (OPS-987):
- Why did conntrack/NAT mappings concentrate CI flows to the same node subset? Is there affinity in upstream NAT gateway?
- Was there any cloud provider maintenance or placement rebalancing coincident with the time window?
- Evaluate whether soft-affinity weight values need a safe-guard clamp in scheduler config to avoid >X influence on score.

Appendix: quick artifacts collected
- Affinity heatmap (compressed): s3://redwood-ops-artifacts/ops-987/heatmap-2026-03-09-0344.png
- Scheduler logs excerpt: s3://redwood-ops-artifacts/ops-987/scheduler-log-excerpt-0340.txt
- Node metric CSV: s3://redwood-ops-artifacts/ops-987/node-metrics-03-38-03-48.csv

Short note for postmortem: this incident was the product of an interaction between a configuration change and noisy traffic. Both weak controls (no canary for scoring changes) and an operational gap (CI running heavy synthetic flows in prod-like pool) contributed. Recommend treating affinity scoring changes as a behavioral change that requires canary and automated drift detection.

(End of notes)
